title: Robust per-tenant export delivery: idempotent retries, schema-drift detection, timezone-aligned CSVs
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background:
Redwood's scheduled usage exports currently surface two classes of customer-impacting failures: 1) repeated webhook redelivery that results in duplicate rows at the customer endpoint and 2) silent schema drift when internal token/field names change resulting in customers failing to ingest CSVs.

Goal:
Deliver a robust, per-tenant export delivery pipeline that ensures idempotent webhook deliveries, a deterministic CSV normalization process (with tenant timezone alignment), and active schema-drift detection with automated owner notifications and safe fallback to S3. This should improve end-to-end reliability and reduce manual incident work for support and infra teams.

Scope (what we'll deliver):
- Idempotency for webhook deliveries: include robust delivery_token, store delivery status in durable queue (per-export idempotency key), and make retries idempotent on redelivery.
- Retry/backoff policy: exponential backoff with full jitter, per-tenant retry budget, TTL and circuit-breaker when endpoint is dead.
- Safe fallback: after N failed webhook attempts (configurable per-tenant), mark export as "delivered-to-s3" and notify tenant via webhook status webhook + optional email. S3 objects follow the existing export naming convention and are accessible via pre-signed URLs for retention window.
- CSV normalization: explicit schema version header (x-export-schema:v1), deterministic column ordering, timezone normalization to tenant-configured tz (or account default UTC), and canonical decimal/date formats. Include a header checksum (X-Export-Header-Hash) to make downstream validation easy.
- Schema-drift detection: compute header signature + sample row fingerprint on every export; compare to canonical schema per tenant and log drift events to exports-schema-drift stream. Trigger automated alerting and open an internal ticket when drift threshold (by occurrence count or field mismatch ratio) is exceeded.
- Observability: metrics (export.delivery.latency, export.delivery.success_rate, export.schema_drift_count, export.fallback_to_s3_count), dashboards, and tracing tags for tenant_id/export_id/delivery_token.
- API/Console: Admin console field to view last-good-schema per tenant, and a one-click rollback to previous schema for CSV producers.

Out of scope: redesign of export manifest format, per-row content transformation for customers, changes to downstream billing logic.

Acceptance criteria:
- Webhook delivery is idempotent for repeated retries using consistent delivery_token (unit + integration tests).
- Configurable per-tenant retry budget is honored and enforced (e2e test with simulated 503s).
- After configured failed attempts, export appears in S3 with valid pre-signed URL and status updated to "fallback_to_s3" (integration test).
- CSVs include x-export-schema header and X-Export-Header-Hash; column ordering stable across repeated exports (compare hashes).
- Schema-drift events emitted to monitoring and appear in the exports-schema-drift dashboard.
- New metrics flow into CloudMetric pipeline and dashboards are added to Console-Observability stack.

Design notes / trade-offs:
- We will add a per-export idempotency table in DynamoDB (small, high write QPS) rather than expanding the existing export queue to avoid long-lived locks. This keeps read/write patterns simple but adds a new operational surface.
- For deterministic CSV column ordering we will maintain a canonical schema record per tenant in the metadata service. Updating the schema will be an explicit update flow (console + API) to avoid silent drift. This requires a one-time migration for tenants that relied on ad-hoc column order previously.
- Fallback-to-S3 is conservative: we will not delete webhook attempts or mark them as permanently failed until S3 copy is confirmed. This increases storage but reduces customer-visible data loss.

Rollout plan:
1) Backend implementation behind feature flag (per-tenant opt-in): idempotency table, retry policy, CSV header & hash.
2) Canary to internal tenants and a small set of customers (5) with high-volume exports. Monitor metrics for 48h.
3) Enable automatic fallback-to-S3 for canary tenants and validate delivery.
4) Update Console with schema viewer and per-tenant toggle.
5) Gradual ramp to all tenants over 2 weeks with monitoring and rollback steps defined.

Telemetry & runbook pointers:
- Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/exports/exports-delivery-overview
- Drift stream / logs: https://kibana.redwood.internal/app/discover#/exports-schema-drift
- Runbook (draft): https://confluence.redwood.internal/display/PLAT/Export+Delivery+Runbook

Security & privacy considerations:
- S3 pre-signed URLs will be short-lived and logged. Exports will continue to honor tenant retention and redaction rules.
- Delivery tokens must be unpredictable (crypto-rand 128-bit) and not leak in logs except in controlled debug mode flagged in audit logs.

Estimated effort and team needs:
- Backend engineers: 2 (4 sprints total split: 2 for core, 1 for S3 fallback/telemetry, 1 for Console/QA)
- QA: 1 (integration + e2e tests)
- Devops/Infra: 1 (SLA dashboards, table provisioning)

Notes: we should coordinate with Support to create a canned postmortem template for drift incidents and a migration plan for customers who need schema remediation.
